description: Composite, three-panel methods figure mixing a process schematic, two photographs/insets and four condition plots. (a) is a Temperature (°C) versus Time (s) schedule of the hot-compression test: a cylindrical specimen labelled 6 mm × 9 mm goes through 'Pretightening', 'Heating' at 10 °C/s, 'Holding 180s at 1250°C', cooling at 10 °C/s, 'Holding 60s' and 'Compressing' to 'True strain: 0.9'; an inset photograph shows the sample clamped between the upper and lower 'In-denter press' jaws with a thermocouple wire welded on. A downstream branch shows 'Water quenching', then 'Side section' cutting feeding 'OLYMPUS GX71' 'Optical observation' and 'SU5000' 'EBSD observation'. (b) stacks two Strain rate (s⁻¹) versus True strain (0–1.0) plots at 'Temperature: 950°C', 'Strain rate controlled by indenter speed': upper — ε̇_I=0.1s⁻¹ transiently decreased at ε_I=0.2 to ε̇_II=0.01s⁻¹; lower — ε̇_I=0.01s⁻¹ transiently increased at ε_I=0.4 to ε̇_II=0.1s⁻¹; both run to ε_total=0.9. (c) stacks two Temperature (°C) versus True strain plots at 'Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹' in which temperature is ramped at 10 °C/s between T_I=1050°C and T_II=950°C in both directions, over strain intervals near 0.4 and near 0.2–0.3. The figure defines the varying-condition matrix (strain-rate steps at 0.2/0.4 strain; temperature ramps at 0.2–0.3/0.4–0.5 strain) that the DRX model is tested against.

subfigures.description: Process schematic: Temperature (°C) vs Time (s) profile of the Gleeble hot-compression procedure for a 6 mm × 9 mm cylinder — Pretightening, Heating at 10 °C/s, Holding 180 s at 1250 °C, cooling at 10 °C/s, Holding 60 s, Compressing to true strain 0.9, then Water quenching. Two photographic insets: the specimen clamped between 'In-denter press' jaws with a thermocouple, and a quenched puck cut into a 'Side section' for 'OLYMPUS GX71' optical and 'SU5000' EBSD observation.

Two stacked Strain rate (s⁻¹) vs True strain plots at Temperature: 950 °C, annotated 'Strain rate controlled by indenter speed'. Upper: ε̇_I = 0.1s⁻¹ held then transiently decreased at ε_I = 0.2 to ε̇_II = 0.01s⁻¹, ending at ε_total = 0.9. Lower: ε̇_I = 0.01s⁻¹ held then transiently increased at ε_I = 0.4 to ε̇_II = 0.1s⁻¹, ending at ε_total = 0.9.

Two stacked Temperature (°C) vs True strain plots at Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹. Upper: T_I = 1050 °C→T_II = 950 °C and T_I = 950 °C→T_II = 1050 °C transitions at 10 °C/s around ε_I ≈ 0.4. Lower: the same two temperature ramps but occurring over the strain range ≈0.2–0.3. Both traces end at ε_total = 0.9.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a Temperature (°C) versus Time (s) schematic showing the hot-compression route: Pretightening → Heating at 10 °C/s → Holding 180s at 1250°C → cooling at 10 °C/s → Holding 60s → Compressing, with the compression segment labelled 'True strain: 0.9'.

The specimen drawn in panel (a) is a cylinder annotated 6 mm (diameter) and 9 mm (height), and a photographic inset shows it clamped between the upper and lower 'In-denter press' jaws with a thermocouple wire attached.

Panel (a) continues into 'Water quenching' followed by 'Side section' extraction, after which the two characterisation routes 'OLYMPUS GX71' optical observation and 'SU5000' EBSD observation are shown.
Both sub-plots of panel (b) are at 'Temperature: 950°C' and carry the note 'Strain rate controlled by indenter speed'; the strain-rate axis runs 0.00–0.10 s⁻¹ and the true-strain axis 0.0–1.0.
Upper sub-plot of (b): strain rate is held at ε̇_I = 0.1s⁻¹ and is 'Transient decrease'd at ε_I = 0.2 down to ε̇_II = 0.01s⁻¹, which continues to ε_total = 0.9 ('Transient decrease' label).
Lower sub-plot of (b): strain rate is held at ε̇_I = 0.01s⁻¹ and is 'Transient increase'd at ε_I = 0.4 up to ε̇_II = 0.1s⁻¹, continuing to ε_total = 0.9.

Both sub-plots of panel (c) are at 'Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹' and show pairs of traces labelled T_I = 1050°C and T_I = 950°C switching to T_II = 950°C and T_II = 1050°C respectively, with the ramps annotated '10°C/s'.
In the upper sub-plot of (c) the temperature transition (black dot ε_I) occurs at a true strain of about 0.4; in the lower sub-plot it occurs at a lower strain, about 0.2–0.3.

The caption states that (b) gives experimental conditions for transient strain-rate variation at 0.2 or 0.4 strains and (c) gives conditions for continuous temperature variation at strain ranges of 0.2–0.3 or 0.4–0.5.

The citing text states the tests used Gleeble 1500 thermomechanical simulator specimens of a low-alloy steel with composition (wt.%) 0.398 C, 0.87 Mn, 0.31 Si, 0.024 S, 0.01 P, 0.05 Ni, 0.16Cr, 0.01 W, 0.1 V, 0.03 Mo, 0.002 Ti, 0.13 Cu and rem. Fe.

The citing text states specimens were cylindrical ϕ 6 mm × 9 mm cut along the rolling direction from hot-rolled round bars, with 0.1 mm tantalum foil placed between the specimen ends and the indenter to prevent interfacial melting and minimise friction.

The citing text states samples were heated to 1250 °C at 10 °C/s and held 180 s for austenite homogenisation, then cooled to the deformation temperature at 10 °C/s and held 60 s; constant-condition tests covered 850–1150 °C and 0.01–10 s⁻¹.

The citing text states each specimen was water quenched immediately after deformation to freeze the high-temperature microstructure, and the side section was analysed by optical microscopy and EBSD (PAG reconstruction).

The figure's overall argument is that it defines the deformation matrix — two strain-rate step conditions at 950 °C and two continuous temperature-ramp conditions at 0.01 s⁻¹, all to ε_total = 0.9 — that the DRX cellular-automaton predictions are validated against.

unreadable_items: panel (a) insets: the photographs of the indenter press and of the characterisation instruments are small/low-resolution, so only the overlaid labels ('In-denter press', 'Sample', 'OLYMPUS GX71', 'SU5000') are readable, not the equipment details

panel (c): the exact strain values at which the temperature ramps start and end cannot be read precisely from the axis; only approximate positions (≈0.4 and ≈0.2–0.3) are visible, the caption supplying the ranges 0.2–0.3 and 0.4–0.5
